key_insight: TI-SAE turns a predictive model’s internal representations into reusable clinical concepts defined by when they occur and which variables they involve.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help researchers inspect what electronic health record models learn, without establishing clinical utility or safety.
method: Learn a shared concept dictionary from a frozen predictive model’s representations.
Define concepts using temporal Gaussian islands and sparse variable combinations.
Use a separate selector to identify concepts driving each patient’s prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered five backbone architectures on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, with three prediction tasks per dataset; the abstract reports strong faithfulness performance without numerical results.
watch_item: Concept dictionaries are backbone-specific, and faithfulness benchmarks alone do not establish clinical validity or generalizability.
paper_title: Temporal Island Sparse Autoencoders for Interpreting Clinical Time-Series Models
